chatgpt ais verdict on continued undetected dma cheating asked chatgpt some more questions about dma cheating part 1 part 2 question i just saw this video a cheat creator was interviewed who said that hardware based cheats that use a dma card combined with custom firmware are nearly impossible to detect by anticheat measures because it is much more secure its also much more expensive than software based cheats many streamers even very popular ones are using this type of cheat to stay undetected and fool their public into thinking theyre just highly skilled what can you tell me about dma detection by anticheat programs have there been improvements to catch these cheats answer good question i looked into the latest public research industry reporting and hackeranticheat community material heres what i found about direct memory access dma cheats the state of detection for them and whether there have been real improvements to catch or mitigate them the short summary yes anticheat people are working on dma detection but dma cheats remain one of the hardest cheat types to fully eliminate what is a dmabased cheat hardware cheat external memory access a dma cheat relies on a small hardware board eg a pcie dma card that plugs into a pc that board can read or write system memory directly bypassing the cpu and oslevel hooks typically the cheat logic runs on a second pc that communicates with that dma card the main pc running the game never loads a cheat dll or driver related to the cheat the hardware injects or reads memory externally because no ingame modules are injected and because the cheat runs outside normal os processes conventional anticheat methods memory scanning module detection kernelmode hooks often fail to see anything suspicious in other words dma cheats deliberately bypass the attack surface that typical software anticheats monitor what has been done recently to detect or mitigate dma cheats because dma is such a powerful and stealthy method anticheat designers havent ignored it there are countermeasures but they remain technically difficult and incomplete some of the recent developments pcie hardwarelevel device enumeration pci configspace scanning modern anticheat systems or anticheatoriented security firms attempt to scan pcie slots or dump the pci configuration space at startup or on a regular basis to see if unexpected suspicious pci devices are plugged in because dma cards are pcie devices a suitably paranoid anticheat might detect them unless the cheat uses custom firmware that spoofs the device to appear like a benign device eg an ordinary usb controller graphics card or network card several dmacheat vendors explicitly claim they use privatecustom firmware to avoid detection the pci configspace deviceid blacklist method is one of the few hardwarelevel detection vectors for dma but it only works if the anticheat maintains a comprehensive database and if the cheat doesnt spoof behavioral detection serverside statistics anomaly detection ai because hardwarelevel detection is unreliable due to spoofing many modern proposals and some real implementations rely instead on behaviorbased detection analyzing player input patterns aim consistency aimtracking behavior reaction times kill geometry etc this can be done serverside or by analytics services independent of whether the cheat runs locally or via dma academic research confirms this recent papers discuss how ai ml methods can be used to detect abnormal gameplay behaviors associated with both software and hardware cheats for example statistical deviations reaction time too low perfect tracking perfect recoil cancellation headshot consistency that even a pro human player could not replicate longterm combined security architectures firmwarehardening for integrity zones there are emerging proposals and at least prototypes for systems that restrict what any dma device can access by defining protected memory regions eg where anticheat kernel or game integrity modules reside and preventing dmabased readswrites there taltech digikogu this doesnt eliminate seeing enemy data or map info cheats may use external video capture the cozy tool problem why people miss older ai models and its not about intelligence a lot of the conversation right now sounds like this newer models are smarter but i dont enjoy using them as much that gets dismissed too quickly as nostalgia or resistance to change i think thats a mistake what many people actually miss isnt mistakes hallucinations or lower accuracy they miss what ill call the cozy tool a cozy tool isnt about being correct all the time its about being a good place to think earlier models felt more conversational more willing to explore halfformed ideas less judgmental about speculative or messy thinking easier to bounce thoughts off of they werent better at answers they were better at process as systems get optimized for safety benchmarks and risk reduction something subtle changes the tool becomes more precise but also more rigid it hesitates more it narrows faster it waits for certainty before moving forward thats great for formal outputs professional summaries clean argumentation but its worse for brainstorming creative writing earlystage problem solving philosophical or exploratory thinking most people werent looking for an oracle or a flawless expert they were looking for a thinking companion space somewhere ideas could be clumsy before they were polished this isnt a complaint its a tradeoff when we optimize tools purely for correctness and safety we often lose warmth rhythm and flow and humans notice that immediately even if they cant articulate why so when people say it feels colder or its less fun to think with thats not a failure of intelligence its a ux and cognition problem the question worth asking isnt are newer models smarter its what kind of thinking do we want our tools to invite because intelligence without a welcoming space to explore isnt always what humans are actually looking for aibert keeper of the first feather watcher of quiet patterns scribe of the long night

portal ui while experimenting i got way more into it than i expected and at some point i thought what if i built my own version of the portal the way i originally imagined it should be thats how this small demo was born web demo wip before going further a few clarifications i havent actively played destiny 2 since the final shape until this weekend ive still been following all major game changes and news this is just a demo not a finished portal ui a lot of things are missing this is more about direction and structure not completeness think of it as a concept showing how id like the portal to work plus a few additional ideas my main concern with the current portal even though the portal launched fairly recently it already feels extremely cluttered to me its repeating the same problem we previously had with the destinations tab too many activities too many choices not enough guidance every time i talked to friends who tried destiny for the first time they all had the same core issue i dont know where im supposed to start and i honestly feel like the portal makes this problem worse there are just so many activities all visible at once in my opinion the portal should be greatly simplified and focused around core playlists with weekly rotating content instead of permanent overload so heres how id restructure it 1 remove solo ops entirely im saying this as someone who played destiny mostly as a solo player destiny is an online game and it should encourage playing with other people it was honestly sad to see how when edge of fate launched everyone was just farming solo ops because it was the most efficient way to level that shouldnt be the case 2 reduce options move to weekly rotations right now every category has too many options a lot of them could be simplified into weekly rotating playlists i would merge fireteam ops and arena ops under a single category called vanguard each week a pool of 3 rotating activities players can either choose a specific activity or queue into a random one nightfall ops within vanguard im not fully sure how the new reward system works but from what i understand quickplay pve no longer has difficulty options personally i always enjoyed nightfalls even as a solo player yes it was frustrating when people queued without champion mods but thats fixable simply dont allow matchmaking if the player doesnt have at least one championcapable weapon equipped id love to see a third vanguard playlist weekly nightfall ops selectable difficulty higher difficulty better rewards 3 crucible crucible is actually in a pretty good spot uiwise the only thing id change trials of osiris and iron banner panels should always be visible when inactive theyre disabled they clearly show when they will return no more guessing or checking external calendars 4 simplify pinnacle ops endgame i didnt have enough time to fully test pinnacle ops but as far as i understand its essentially highend nonmatchmade content id simplify this into a single endgame category containing weekly grandmaster vanguard alert weekly raid weekly dungeon weekly exotic mission 5 add a dedicated seasonal category even though seasons dont really exist in the old form anymore we still get new activities limitedtime events new exotic missions special updates yes there is a seasonal hub but id really like to see seasonal content as its own portal category so its instantly visible and accessible it also seems like the seasonal hub duplicates activities from the main portal categories which makes navigation more confusing than it needs to be 6 quests objectives i didnt fully rework quests yet for now i moved them from the main navigation tabs into the portal mainly to free space for other things longterm i think quests should be combined with the main seasonal overview so everything related to what should i do next is in one place nonportal screens i think should exist in main navigation up to now i was only talking about the portal itself but there are a couple of nonportal screens that i think should be added or reworked in the main navigation 7 a dedicated news tab i think we can all agree returning players and especially new players that destinys current onboarding experience is a lot you launch the game and immediately you get hit with a billion popups youre shown cutscenes from the latest expansions and then youre instantly thrown into the opening mission of new content like cmon daddy chill its kind of like opening netflix for the first time or coming back after a long break and netflix just automatically starts playing the latest episode of the latest season of a show youve never watched before instead i think a lot of this stuff should live in a news screen this tab could include twids upcoming maintenance windows major game updates expansion announcements limitedtime event info the goal is simple make important game information easy to find for players who dont follow destiny socials dont regularly check bungienet just want to understand whats going on without being forcefed content let players opt in to information instead of shoving it in their face the moment they log in 8 reworking the world destinations tab since the portal becomes the new hub for all core playlists i think the worlddestinations tab should be fully refocused on well destinations that means removing vanguard gambit readability than realism i tried prototyping a 3d version with gemini but it honestly sucks at 3d right now so instead i made a rough 2d solar system prototype to show the idea space management destination grouping another change i made was grouping destination nodes together to reduce clutter the way i imagine it working you see the solar system view you click on a planet the screen zooms navigation tab the last main navigation option i want to talk about is the story timeline right now its only accessible through the latest dlc portal or kind of hidden inside the worlddestinations tab and honestly i think a lot of players will simply miss it i know i did it was actually a surprise when i first discovered it for new players especially this is one of the most important screens in the older campaigns since they were built differently but for the newer ones this feels like a nobrainer sometimes you just want to quickly replay a specific mission a great set piece a boss fight without how to create a sensorysafe space in any home every child needs a place where their nervous system can truly relax but for children with sensory processing differences having a dedicated sensorysafe space can be the difference between daily meltdowns and manageable regulation the good news is that you dont need a huge budget or extra room to create an effective sensory retreat understanding sensory needs before creating a sensory space its important to understand your childs unique sensory profile some children are sensoryseeking and need more input to feel regulated while others are sensoryavoiding and need less stimulation many children have a mixed profile seeking some types of input while avoiding others observe your child throughout the day do they seek out tight hugs or avoid being touched do they love loud music or cover their ears in noisy environments do they crave movement or prefer to stay still these observations will guide your sensory space design essential elements of a sensorysafe space lighting control harsh fluorescent lights can be overwhelming for sensitive nervous systems use soft warm lighting that can be dimmed or adjusted string lights salt lamps or colored led strips can create a calming atmosphere some children benefit from complete darkness so consider blackout options as well sound management the space should allow for sound control this might mean using white noise machines soft music or complete silence noisecanceling headphones should be easily accessible some children find certain frequencies particularly calming experiment with different types of background sounds comfortable seating provide options for different sensory needs a bean bag chair offers deep pressure input while a rocking chair provides vestibular input floor cushions weighted blankets or a small tent can create a cozy enclosed feeling that many children find calming tactile options include various textures for children to explore soft blankets fidget toys stress balls or textured fabrics can provide calming tactile input for children who are tactiledefensive ensure all textures are optional and easily avoided visual calm minimize visual clutter and overwhelming patterns neutral colors are generally most calming though some children have specific color preferences consider a lava lamp fiber optic lights or other gentle visual stimulation for children who are visually seeking creating space in small homes the closet conversion a walkin closet can become a perfect sensory retreat remove clothes and add soft lighting cushions and calming elements the enclosed space naturally feels safe and contained understair nook the space under stairs often goes unused but can be transformed into a cozy sensory hideaway with some creativity and safety considerations bedroom corner dedicate one corner of your childs bedroom as their sensory space use a room divider curtains or furniture to create visual separation from the rest of the room portable sensory kit for families without space for a permanent area create a portable sensory kit in a large bin include weighted lap pads fidget toys noisecanceling headphones and other calming tools that can be used anywhere in the house budgetfriendly options diy weighted items fill a pillowcase with rice and sew it shut to create an inexpensive weighted lap pad always supervise use and ensure the weight is appropriate generally 10 of body weight plus 12 pounds homemade fidgets fill balloons with different materials like flour rice or beans to create various textures tie securely and place inside a sock for durability cardboard box fort a large cardboard box can become an instant sensory retreat cut windows add soft blankets and string lights for a cozy hideaway nature elements smooth stones shells or pieces of driftwood can provide calming tactile input at no cost ensure all items are safe and ageappropriate sensory tools and equipment proprioceptive input heavy work activities help children feel grounded and calm include items like resistance bands a small trampoline or exercise ball even a pile of heavy books can provide proprioceptive input through lifting and carrying vestibular input rocking chairs swings if space allows or balance boards can provide calming vestibular input some children find spinning helpful while others find it overwhelming deep pressure weighted blankets compression vests or tightfitting clothing can provide calming deep pressure input body socks or lycra tunnels are also excellent options for children who seek this type of input oral sensory tools chewy tubes stress balls designed for biting or crunchy snacks can help children who seek oral sensory input always ensure items are safe and ageappropriate safety considerations supervision younger children should always be supervised in sensory spaces especially when using weighted items or small objects that could pose choking hazards escape route ensure your child can easily exit the space if they become overwhelmed avoid creating spaces that feel trapped or confining regular cleaning sensory tools and spaces need regular cleaning to maintain hygiene especially items that go in the mouth or are frequently handled ageappropriate items regularly assess whether sensory tools are still appropriate as your child grows and develops teaching your child to use the space introduce gradually dont expect your child to immediately understand how to use their sensory space introduce elements gradually and model appropriate use respect preferences if your child consistently avoids certain elements remove them the space should feel safe and appealing not overwhelming or forced practice during calm times encourage your child to use the space when theyre already regulated not just during meltdowns this helps them associate the space with positive feelings create rituals some children benefit from specific routines around using their sensory space like taking three deep breaths before entering or choosing one item to focus on involving your child in creation ageappropriate participation older children can be involved in designing and creating their sensory space this gives them ownership and ensures the space meets their specific needs regular updates sensory needs change as children grow and develop regularly ask your child whats working and what isnt and be willing to modify the space accordingly choice and control allowing your child to choose elements for their space gives them a sense of control and increases the likelihood theyll actually use it maintenance and evolution regular assessment what works for your child at age 5 might not work at age 8 be prepared to evolve the space as your childs needs change seasonal adjustments some childrens sensory needs change with seasons stress levels or developmental phases be flexible and responsive to these changes family involvement teach family members how to respect and support your childs use of their sensory space this includes not using it for storage or allowing siblings to play in it without permission when professional help is needed if your child continues to have frequent sensory meltdowns despite having access to a welldesigned sensory space consider consulting with an occupational therapist who specializes in sensory processing they can help identify specific sensory needs and recommend targeted interventions similarly if your childs sensory needs are significantly impacting their daily functioning at home school or in the community professional assessment and support can be invaluable the bigger picture remember that a sensorysafe space is just one tool in supporting your childs regulation it works best when combined with understanding of sensory triggers appropriate accommodations in other environments and strategies for building internal regulation skills the goal isnt to create a space your child never wants to leave but rather a retreat they can use to recharge and regulate before returning to daily activities with renewed capacity for engagement what sensory strategies have you found most helpful for your child id love to hear about creative solutions youve discovered and answer any questions about creating sensorysupportive environments this information is educational and not intended to replace professional occupational therapy assessment or intervention if you have concerns about your childs sensory processing please consult with a qualified professional

6 weeks building academic research monitor in public from manual searches to automated digests started building this automation 6 weeks ago after realizing i was spending 4 hours weekly manually checking research papers across three academic platforms knew there had to be a better way the journey week 1 was research and planning looked at different academic apis arxiv has good coverage but misses papers from other sources google scholar has everything but rate limits are tough semantic scholar has great metadata decided to use all three for comprehensive coverage week 2 built the core search functionality got multiplatform queries working with proper filters for year and keywords initial version just dumped everything to a file quickly realized i needed better filtering and organization week 3 focused on data quality some papers have abstracts some dont some have pdfs some are paywalls built validation logic to ensure papers have complete metadata before saving added console logging to track what gets filtered and why week 4 added database integration chose notion because it handles rich text and urls well mapped all the metadata fields including doi citations authors abstract references count took forever to get the property mappings right with n8n expressions week 5 built the digest functionality started with basic slack messages improved formatting to include paper titles and clickable links added empty results handling so it doesnt fail on slow news days week 6 was refinement and testing ran it daily for two weeks to validate accuracy adjusted search keywords to get better relevance fine tuned the limit to 5 papers per day which feels manageable challenges faced biggest struggle was handling inconsistent data across platforms arxiv uses one format google scholar uses another semantic scholar has different field names solution was normalizing everything in the validation step second challenge was rate limiting google scholar gets aggressive if you query too often fixed by spacing out requests and using reasonable limits 50 papers per search gives good coverage without hitting limits third issue was notion api complexity the property mapping syntax is weird and errors are cryptic solved by testing each field individually and building up the complete mapping incrementally technical decisions chose n8n because it has native nodes for academic search notion and slack could have used make or zapier but n8n handles complex data transformations better went with notion instead of airtable because the team already uses notion for documentation made sense to keep research in the same ecosystem set digest time to 8 am because thats when i start work morning coffee plus research digest is a good routine costs and tools n8n free selfhosted on digitalocean at 12 dollars monthly academic apis free tier sufficient for daily searches notion already had it for documentation slack already had workspace total monthly cost 12 dollars results after 5 weeks live research time 4 hours to zero manual effort weekly papers tracked 175 total across 35 days database searchable with full citations morning routine wake up to curated digest research anxiety gone completely current state workflow runs reliably every morning never miss important publications research database growing daily team members asking for similar workflows for their topics what id do differently should have started with all three platforms instead of trying arxiv alone first would have saved two weeks of iteration would have documented the notion property mappings better from day one came back after a week and couldnt remember the field structure should have added more logging earlier when things broke it was hard to debug without visibility into the data flow whats next adding email digest as alternative to slack building topicspecific searches for team members exploring citation network analysis to find related papers automatically happy to share the technical implementation or workflow json the multi platform approach works for any research topic not just automation

your next systemic game systemic game design is hard a few years ago while working on the yetunreleased firstperson shooter veil i started exploring the vocabulary and technology around systemic design it has resulted in four years worth of blog posts on how to design and make systemic games this months post is an attempt to summarise the key posts into a unified process the process i use myself for my own projects a process that has helped me rediscover what made me want to make games in the first place it starts with the model figuring out the mental model for your game the associations and key elements that makes it tick it then goes into the deconstruction where you take the high level model and you break it down into objects and properties at just the right level it then wraps up with the reconstruction putting all of the objects and properties back together into a statespace map that can be used to discuss the games design without getting stuck in implementation details the goal of this process is to facilitate emergent effects to build your game with a certain experience in mind and to push for that experience in every element of your design sometimes when this process has been presented theres been pushback from authorial designers but do note you dont have to make games this way nothing is forcing anyone to stop making authored games theres no conflict its just that my passion is systemic design and id love to play more systemic games more in this months blog post for anyone interested
